issues.body:
Every new fixture either yields a non-empty result or is expected to raise. Nothing asserts the third outcome the function must support: the provenance directory EXISTS on the ledger but holds no record for this repo yet (in production, a fresh ledger carrying only `orchestration/provenance/README.md`), which must return an empty set quietly.

Today the code is correct — the README satisfies `any(path.startswith(prefix))` and the loop matches nothing. But the property is unpinned: mutating the new guard from "no entry under the directory" to "no matching record" (e.g. moving it after the loop as `if not numbers: raise`) keeps the main `{685}` check green and keeps the renamed-directory check green, while turning a genuinely-empty ledger into a fatal census. Given this raise is brand new and is the fix for round-1 major #2, its boundary is worth one line.
issues.fix_hint:
Add one case asserting the quiet-empty outcome, e.g.:

    check("...and a present-but-empty provenance directory reads as 'nothing recorded'",
          recorded_pr_numbers(repo, "reg/istry", worker_pr,
                              read_tree=lambda: {"truncated": False,
                                                 "tree": [{"path": "orchestration/provenance/README.md",
                                                           "type": "blob"}]}),
          set())

This distinguishes "the directory is gone" (raise) from "the directory is there and empty" (set()), which is exactly the pair the new guard exists to separate.
issues.title: The legitimate "directory present, zero records" path returns set() but is not pinned, so the new presence guard could be tightened into a false fail-closed unnoticed

issues.body:
The old read placed the ref in the query string (`contents/{directory}?ref={LEDGER_REF}`); the new one interpolates it as a path segment ahead of the query (`git/trees/{LEDGER_REF}?recursive=1`). `LEDGER_REF` is `os.environ.get("REGISTRY_LEDGER_REF", "ledger")` (scripts/worker-pr.py:418) and is unquoted in both, but in path position a value containing `?` or `#` can now rewrite the query — e.g. `REGISTRY_LEDGER_REF="ledger?recursive=0&x="` would silently drop recursion.

Deliberately filed as a nit, not higher: the value is operator-supplied workflow configuration rather than untrusted input, the unquoted pattern is pre-existing here, and the outcome now fails CLOSED anyway — a non-recursive tree lists only top-level entries, nothing starts with `orchestration/provenance/`, and the new presence guard raises. Noting it only because `scripts/pat-validity.py:659,669` already quotes this same constant with `urllib.parse.quote(LEDGER_REF, safe='')`, so the repo has a house style this line diverges from.
issues.fix_hint: Match pat-validity.py: `f"repos/{registry_repo}/git/trees/{urllib.parse.quote(worker_pr.LEDGER_REF, safe='')}?recursive=1"` (the module already imports `urllib.parse` at pat-validity's call sites; add the import here if absent). The existing endpoint-wiring self-test pins the default `ledger`, which quotes to itself, so it stays green.
issues.title: `worker_pr.LEDGER_REF` moved from query-string position to path-segment position without URL quoting

verdict.summary:
All five round-1 findings are addressed, and the two majors are fixed at the mechanism level rather than papered over.

(1) MAJOR #1 (untested directory-scoping guard) is killed properly. `_listing` now carries three decoys whose basename matches this repo's stem but which must NOT count: `orchestration/provenance-archive/o--r--pr686.json` (sibling directory — note `startswith("orchestration/provenance/")` is False because the next char is `-`, so this is a real prefix-boundary decoy, not a trivially-different one), a bare `o--r--pr686.json` at repo root, and `orchestration/provenance/sub/o--r--pr686.json` (in-directory but nested). Expectation stays `{685}`. Mutating `name = path[len(prefix):] if ... startswith(prefix)` to `path.rpartition('/')[2]` now yields `{685, 686}` and reds. The newly load-bearing line is no longer vacuous.

(2) MAJOR #2 (false fail-closed docstring) is fixed by restoring the property rather than deleting the claim: the new `if not any(... path.startswith(prefix))` raise means a renamed/moved `PROVENANCE_DIR` reds instead of returning `set()`, so "the layout moved" and "nothing is recorded" are again distinct answers. Pinned non-vacuously by the `renamed/provenance/README.md` case (delete the guard and the `else` branch fires). Steady state stays quiet because the ledger branch is cut from master, which tracks `orchestration/provenance/README.md`.

(3) MINOR #3: the `not isinstance(response, dict)` arm is now covered by `read_tree=lambda: None` (removing the arm raises AttributeError, not MintError -> red) and `{"message": "Not Found"}`.

(4) MINOR #4: `type == "blob"` filter added, pinned by the `{path: .../pr687.json, type: "tree"}` fixture — drop the filter and the result becomes `{685, 687}`.

(5) NIT #5: `prefix` hoisted above the loop.

The endpoint-wiring pin (`repos/reg/istry/git/trees/ledger?recursive=1`, `_gh_json` patched via module globals and restored in `finally`) survives. `truncated is not False` remain… [truncated 364 chars]
